extra.message: The /api/search handler reflects the raw, unvalidated query parameter req.query.searchTerm directly back to the client with res.status(200).send(req.query.searchTerm). Express sends a string with a text/html Content-Type, so a request such as /api/search?searchTerm=<script>alert(1)</script> returns executable HTML (reflected XSS).

extra.message: Attacker-controlled data is read from the URL fragment via $location.hash() and stored in $scope.searchTerm, then passed to search(). Because the app runs in HTML5 mode the fragment is fully user controlled, so a crafted link like /xss-search#<script>...</script> drives the XSS sink at line 35.

extra.message: GET /api/user/profile returns the profile keyed only by the client-supplied cookie req.cookies.userAuthToken. There is no session validation or authorization check, and the token is a constant (see line 53), so any unauthenticated attacker can supply the known token and read any user's profile (broken access control / missing authentication).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST /api/user/profile writes arbitrary req.body into data.profile[req.cookies.userAuthToken] with no authentication or ownership check. Because the auth token is a hardcoded constant known to everyone, an unauthenticated attacker can overwrite any user's profile.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The cookie value is used as a property key with no key validation: data.profile[user] = req.body where user = req.cookies.userAuthToken. An attacker can send Cookie: userAuthToken=__proto__ and a JSON body, causing the __proto__ setter to be invoked and polluting the prototype of the data.profile object (prototype pollution).

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: State-changing endpoints POST /user/profile (and /user/login, /user/logout) authenticate solely via the userAuthToken cookie and implement no anti-CSRF token or Origin/Referer validation. A malicious site can submit a cross-site form to /api/user/profile and change the victim's profile, as demonstrated by attacker-app/csrf-attack.html.

The random session token generation is disabled and replaced with a hardcoded literal: randomNumber = '35592211433686316'. Every login receives the same predictable token, making session hijacking and authentication bypass trivial.

The authentication cookie is set without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite flags: res.cookie('userAuthToken', randomNumber, {maxAge: 3600000, path: '/'}). The session token is readable by client-side JavaScript, enabling theft via XSS and cross-site transmission.

The authentication token and profile contents are written to the server log: console.log('User Requesting Read: ', req.cookies.userAuthToken) and console.log('Profile found: ', data.profile[...]). Session tokens and personal data exposed in logs can be harvested by anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: No X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors header is set; the only CSP middleware is commented out. The application can therefore be embedded in an attacker-controlled iframe and clickjacked, as demonstrated by attacker-app/clickjacking-attack.html framing /clickjacking.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: In the default (dev) environment the entire repository root is exposed as static files with app.use(express.static('./')). This allows unauthenticated retrieval of server source code (e.g. /src/server/routes.js, including the hardcoded token), package.json, gulpfile.js, and other project files (information exposure).

cwe: CWE-538: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory

extra.message: The X-Powered-By header is not disabled (app.disable('x-powered-by') is commented out), disclosing the Express/Node stack to attackers and aiding targeted exploitation.
